identity.title: EditVerse: Unifying Image and Video Editing and Generation with In-Context Learning

problem.claim: Unify image and video generation and editing in one model.

gap.claim: Video generation and editing remain fragmented because of architectural limitations and data scarcity.

contributions.claim: EditVerse represents text, images, and videos as one token sequence to support in-context learning, cross-modal transfer, and variable-resolution or variable-duration inputs and outputs.
A scalable pipeline curates 232K video-editing samples and combines them with large image and video datasets for joint training.
EditVerseBench is presented as a benchmark for instruction-based video editing across diverse tasks and resolutions.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe EditVerseBench as the first benchmark for instruction-based video editing.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments and user studies show state-of-the-art performance, surpassing existing open-source and commercial models.
The authors report emergent editing and generation abilities across modalities.

narrative_sequence.summary: Image generation and editing have moved toward unified frameworks, whereas video generation and editing remain fragmented.
The paper introduces EditVerse, unifying image and video generation and editing through shared multimodal token sequences and self-attention.
It addresses video-editing data scarcity with a 232K-sample pipeline and introduces EditVerseBench for instruction-based video editing.
The authors report strong experimental and user-study results, including comparisons with open-source and commercial models and cross-modal emergent abilities.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links a unified token representation to cross-modal transfer and flexible input/output handling, then pairs the framework with a targeted data pipeline for video editing.

lessons.interpretation: A representation change may be more persuasive when its claimed capabilities are matched with data construction that directly targets the main bottleneck.
lessons.application: For a multimodal paper, connect each architectural claim to a concrete training-data strategy addressing the modality or task limitation.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the proposed representation and data pipeline are not independently separable or when the bottleneck is not data-related.

unknowns: No quantitative metrics, dataset splits, baselines, or user-study protocol are provided in the abstract.
The abstract does not specify which editing and generation abilities are emergent or how arbitrary resolutions and durations are operationalized.
